key_insight: AlphaDefect reports expert-level Slay the Spire 2 play using one PPO-trained network per character to handle every combat and noncombat decision.
engineering_relevance: Structured entity representations and engine-computed consequences offer a practical design pattern for agents tackling long-horizon decisions under randomness.
method: Train one network per character with proximal policy optimization (PPO).
Encode cards, relics and enemies using learned identity embeddings, game attributes and public-information consequences.
Evaluate greedy play and test-time search on seeds not used in training.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 62–77% greedy and 68–80% search-assisted win rates across six characters at Ascension 10, after 1.3–6.7 billion training decisions per character; removing identity information yielded no wins, while removing computed consequences reduced wins by 8.3 percentage points.
watch_item: Results depend on substantial training compute and game-engine features; the reported 11–20% human win rates come from uploaded runs across skill levels, not a controlled expert comparison.
paper_title: AlphaDefect: Expert-Level AI for Slay the Spire 2
